newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAELI BONDS END LOWER ON HIGH CPI FEARS.
newsitem.headline: ISRAELI BONDS END LOWER ON HIGH CPI FEARS.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed higher on Wednesday but prices of bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) fell as the market awaited publication of July's consumer price index on Friday, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 pct to 108.69
Volume including Makams was a low 127 million shekels.
"The market is basically waiting to see what July's CPI will be on Friday and whether the central bank will raise interest rates on August 25," Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities said.
He said the market was expecting a high July CPI rise of 1.0 to 1.2 percent which was expected to trigger a 0.5 percentage point rise in the central bank's key lending rate for September.
"Prices of CPI-linked bonds fell today, mainly long bonds, because of fears of an interest rate rise. Also, these bonds made a big move in the last two months and this is a correction," Halpern said.
Yields on CPI-linked long bonds were back up to 3.83 percent, after having fallen to 3.75 percent, he said.

"I assume that if interest rates go up, the yields may rise even more," Halpern said, adding that in the long run the market expected yields on CPI-linked long bonds to resume their fall and reach 3.6 to 3.7 percent by the end of the year.
Yields of CPI-linked bonds have fallen in the last two months on average from 4.2 percent two months ago to 3.6 percent, due to a tight supply of these bonds.
Prices of unlinked bonds and Makams rose on Wednesday because yields on these bonds are attractive, Eyal Segal of United Mizrahi Bank said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
